text: Making API calls is a core skill for modern developers. When you work with an API, your application sends an HTTP request to a server, asking for data or an action. The server usually responds with data in JSON format, which is lightweight and easy for programs to read. However, you often need to prove who you are before the API will respond, so you include an authentication key in your request. It's also important to respect rate limits, meaning you cannot send too many requests in a short time, or you might be blocked. Finally, always plan for error handling. Servers can be slow or unavailable, so your code should check for errors and provide a helpful message instead of crashing.
